# FAA briefly halts flights into Chicago O'Hare, citing staffing at the regional radar approach-control facility

*NBC Chicago, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/ground-stop-issued-at-ohare-airport-due-to-staffing-at-start-of-busy-holiday-week/4020413/>*

NBC Chicago reports that on 23 November the FAA said flights to Chicago O'Hare were held because of staffing, and then that it was briefly pausing flights into O'Hare because of staffing constraints at the Chicago terminal radar approach control facility. According to the report, the stop was lifted by about 12:30 pm.

No cause beyond staffing was given by the FAA.

# FBI release: ISIS Supporter Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Concealing His Role in Creating and Disseminating Terrorist Propaganda Via Social Media

*Federal Bureau of Investigation, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases/isis-supporter-sentenced-to-15-years-in-prison-for-concealing-his-role-in-creating-and-disseminating-terrorist-propaganda-via-social-media>*

The FBI said a man who supported ISIS has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for concealing material support to a foreign terrorist organisation, in a case the release says concerned his role in creating and spreading the group's propaganda on social media.

The email gave no further detail, and the full release on fbi.gov could not be read for this summary; the account is the FBI's own.

# Former Belarusian political prisoner says security officers pressed him to cooperate after release and threatened a longer sentence if he refused

*Zerkalo, 2026-11-23. Original, in Russian: <https://news.zerkalo.io/life/141080.html>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Zerkalo, an independent Belarusian outlet in exile, publishes an interview in which a former political prisoner, convicted over a private chat group after the 2020 protests, says that one to two months before his release KGB officers asked him to sign a pledge and to cooperate with them afterwards, and that when he refused they told him his sentence would be "just the appetizer".

He also describes losing visits and parcels, an untreated injury in the colony, and a court that disregarded an independent linguistic report finding nothing criminal in the chat; he has since left Belarus. This is his account, and no response from the authorities is reported. (Summary translated from the Russian.) (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# Israeli police and security service detain a man suspected of distributing Iranian-directed threat leaflets in Tel Aviv for payment

*i24NEWS, 2026-11-23. Original, in Hebrew: <https://www.i24news.co.il/news/news/defense-news/tel-aviv-threatening-flyers-man-arrested-iran-dire>. Title translated from the Hebrew.*

i24NEWS reports that Israel Police and the Shin Bet say a 69-year-old man was in contact with a hostile party believed to be Iranian and printed and handed out leaflets in north Tel Aviv for 3,000 shekels after answering a number advertised on social media. According to the report, the leaflets carried a QR code to a site linked to an Iran-associated hacker group and warned of attacks on power and desalination plants.

He was released under restrictive conditions and his passport taken; no indictment has been filed, and investigators are examining whether he knew who was behind the order. He is presumed innocent. (Summary translated from the Hebrew.) (Summary translated from the Hebrew.)

# Israel's police shut down operational messaging apps over a feared leak of classified information and order a force-wide password reset

*ynet, 2026-11-23. Original, in Hebrew: <https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/hjkcf7fj7l>. Title translated from the Hebrew.*

Ynet reports that Israel's police described a "complex technological event" that began on 22 November and switched off several applications, including the operational messaging system, out of concern that sensitive and classified information could leak. According to the report, about 100,000 personnel must reset their passwords and the way officers log in is being changed.

The report says a cyberattack is feared but an external fault is also being examined; no cause has been established and no one is named as responsible. (Summary translated from the Hebrew.) (Summary translated from the Hebrew.)

# Leaked Russian death-registration database, which an independent outlet says is genuine, records about 490,000 war deaths by September 2026

*Mediazona, 2026-11-23. Original, in Russian: <https://zona.media/article/2026/11/23/rosstat-leaks>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Mediazona, an independent Russian outlet, reports that hacker groups leaked a statistics-service database of about 11.7 million civil-registry death records from 2021 to September 2026; the groups say one of them is a Belarusian hacktivist collective. Mediazona says it checked the records against named lists of soldiers, court rulings, the inheritance register and official statistics and found matches of about 95–97%.

According to its analysis, about 490,000 military deaths were registered by the end of September 2026, and it estimates around 700,000 once missing and unregistered deaths are counted. No official response is reported. (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# New South Wales assisted-dying board reports 1,419 assisted deaths in 2025–26, up 38%, and no referrals for suspected breaches

*NSW Voluntary Assisted Dying Board, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/voluntary-assisted-dying/Publications/annual-report-2025-2026.pdf>*

The board's third annual report says 2,959 people made a first request for voluntary assisted dying in New South Wales in 2025–26, up 29%, and 2,875 had a first assessment, up 34%. It says 1,419 people died after taking a voluntary-assisted-dying substance, up 38%, and 84.9% had it administered by a practitioner.

In new analysis for 2024–25, the board puts assisted deaths at 1.8% of the 58,714 deaths in the state, using provisional national statistics. It reports making no referrals for suspected breaches of the Act in 2025–26.

# Residents of Moscow and St Petersburg report widespread mobile and home internet failures, including government-approved sites, with no official explanation

*Meduza, 2026-11-23. Original, in Russian: <https://meduza.io/news/2026/11/23/zhiteli-moskvy-i-peterburga-pozhalovalis-chto-u-nih-perestal-rabotat-internet-kak-mobilnyy-tak-i-domashniy>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Meduza, an independent Russian outlet in exile, reports that on the morning of 23 November users in Moscow and St Petersburg complained on outage-tracking services that both mobile and home internet had stopped working, and that some said even sites on the government's "white list" of permitted services could not be reached.

Meduza says the cause is unknown. No statement from the communications regulator is reported; other outlets mention drone-alert restrictions only as an unconfirmed explanation. (Summary translated from the Russian.) (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# Serbian opposition leader alleges the security agency ran a covert hybrid-threats centre that monitored students, journalists and opposition politicians; the agency denies it

*N1, 2026-11-23. Original, in Serbian: <https://n1info.rs/vesti/situacioni-centar-za-hibridne-pretnje-bia/>. Title translated from the Serbian.*

N1 reports that a Serbian opposition party leader told a press conference that the country's Security Information Agency ran a "situation centre for hybrid threats" for about two years, staffed from the police, the military police and military intelligence. According to his account, the centre monitored students, independent journalists, activists and opposition politicians, filmed protests and passed the footage on, and ran a bot unit that logged commenters' IP addresses, device details and locations; he said it stopped work on 19 November and that he will give names to the parliamentary committee that oversees the security services.

N1 notes that the claims have not been independently verified. The agency said its only situation centre was set up lawfully in 2018 and does no field work, called the claims malicious and said it would refer them to the competent authorities. No prosecutor is reported to have acted. (Summary translated from the Serbian.)

# Six Serbian rights groups ask the Supreme Public Prosecutor to decide urgently whether the sound-cannon case continues and which office handles it

*Vreme, 2026-11-23. Original, in Serbian: <https://vreme.com/vesti/nevladine-organizacije-tok-slucaj-zvucni-top/>. Title translated from the Serbian.*

Vreme reports that six Serbian civil-society organisations, among them the Belgrade Centre for Human Rights, Crta and YUCOM, asked the Supreme Public Prosecutor to decide urgently whether the case over the alleged use of a "sound cannon" at the 15 March 2025 Belgrade protest continues and which office should handle it. The groups say neither the First Basic nor the Higher Public Prosecutor's Office in Belgrade can be expected to investigate promptly.

According to the report, they rely on the Supreme Public Prosecutor's commission report of 10 November, which they say found that the Higher office's inquiry was run to confirm officials' claims that nothing happened, and note that the European Court of Human Rights has given the government until 15 January 2027 to answer an application by 35 protesters. Serbian authorities have denied that any such device was used; no response from the prosecutors is reported. (Summary translated from the Serbian.)

# Spain's National Court refuses to reopen charges against a former party leader over the alleged Interior Ministry spying operation on the party's ex-treasurer, as the main trial awaits judgment

*Europa Press, 2026-11-23. Original, in Spanish: <https://www.europapress.es/nacional/noticia-audiencia-nacional-rechaza-imputar-cospedal-pieza-espionaje-barcenas-caso-villarejo-20261123140725.html>. Title translated from the Spanish.*

Europa Press reports that the criminal chamber of Spain's National Court rejected an appeal by the governing Socialist party asking that a former secretary-general of the Partido Popular, her former husband and the party's legal representative be charged, on the strength of three recorded conversations with a retired police commissioner. The case concerns an operation allegedly organised from the Interior Ministry under the previous government to take sensitive material from the party's former treasurer and obstruct a corruption investigation.

According to the report, the court found the newest recordings lacked consistency and criminal relevance and said a case already tried and awaiting judgment cannot be reopened. No verdict has been given in the main trial, and everyone accused is presumed innocent. (Summary translated from the Spanish.) (Summary translated from the Spanish.)

# Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council calls alleged Chinese funding of a local-election candidate a national-security matter and points to AI and facial-recognition data collection

*Central News Agency (Taiwan), 2026-11-23. Original, in Chinese: <https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202611230054.aspx>. Title translated from the Chinese.*

Taiwan's Central News Agency reports that the deputy head of the Mainland Affairs Council said a New Taipei case, in which a local-election candidate was indicted on 21 November under the Anti-Infiltration Act over alleged Chinese funding, shows that Beijing's interference has become a serious national-security issue. According to the agency, he said advances in Chinese AI and facial recognition make such tactics more sophisticated and that data collection may reach beyond elections into daily life.

He said investigators and the National Security Bureau hold specific evidence and will brief the public once the courts take up the case, the report says. The charges are allegations, the defendants are presumed innocent, and the report carries no response from Beijing. (Summary translated from the Chinese.)

# UK data-protection regulator's audit of London police facial recognition makes three urgent recommendations on retrospective searches

*Information Commissioner's Office, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://ico.org.uk/media2/e2bhqkfe/met-police-audit-exec-summary-20261120.pdf>*

The Information Commissioner's Office says its consensual audit of the Metropolitan Police rated both live and retrospective facial recognition as giving "reasonable" assurance, and made 29 recommendations. Three are urgent and all concern retrospective facial recognition, where 11 more are rated high priority.

According to the summary, the force's data protection officer appeared detached from oversight of retrospective searches, the regulator could not gain assurance that probe images are retained lawfully, and searches of the national police database are poorly documented. The ICO describes scope for improvement to reduce the risk of non-compliance, not a finding of breach; the phone-based facial recognition pilot was not assessed because it was not yet operating.

# US Commerce Department adds seven Southeast Asian data-centre firms to its Entity List over the risk of advanced AI chips being diverted to China

*Al Jazeera, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/24/us-adds-megaspeed-firm-at-centre-of-nvidia-scandal-to-export-control-list>*

Al Jazeera reports that the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security added a Singapore data-centre company and six affiliates in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List, saying they were acting contrary to US national security or foreign policy interests; exporting advanced US technology to them now requires a licence.

According to the report, Malaysia's trade ministry said one listed entity is not Malaysian, and the company has previously described itself as a lawful business. No charges have been announced.

# Virginia and Oregon sue an AI chatbot's maker under consumer-protection law over sexualised images, alleging misrepresented safeguards

*KSAT (Associated Press), 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.ksat.com/business/2026/11/23/sexual-images-from-elon-musks-ai-chatbot-harmed-consumers-ags-argue/>*

The Associated Press reports that Virginia's attorney general sued in state court in Richmond, and Oregon filed a separate suit, against SpaceX, X and SpaceX's AI subsidiary over sexualised images generated by its chatbot. According to AP, Virginia alleges the companies misrepresented that they had implemented and enforced safeguards against harmful sexualised imagery, and seeks $2,500 per wilful violation, an injunction and disgorgement.

The company says it tests and adjusts its protections, acts against abusers and reports them to law enforcement. These are civil allegations, not findings.

# White House release: Expeditious Enforcement of Capital Sentences and the Pursuit of Justice for Victims of Heinous Crimes

*The White House, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/11/expeditious-enforcement-of-capital-sentences-and-the-pursuit-of-justice-for-victims-of-heinous-crimes/>*

The White House published a presidential memorandum directing the Attorney General to seek the federal death penalty in certain cases, including the murder of a minor and murders committed during rape, kidnapping or trafficking, according to the memorandum. It also directs that capital appeals and habeas proceedings be prioritised and that administrative delays to federal executions be removed.

These are the administration's directions as published; the memorandum does not decide any case.

# White House release: President [name] Stands with Victims' Families as [name] Grants Mass Clemency to Depraved Killers

*The White House, 2026-11-23. Original: <https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/11/president-trump-stands-with-victims-families-as-newsom-grants-mass-clemency-to-depraved-killers/>*

The White House criticised California's governor for commuting the death sentences of all 548 people on the state's death row, saying victims' families were not told in advance, and it profiled several of the people whose sentences were commuted.

# Australia's parliament passes defence laws creating security zones with arrest, search and drone take-down powers; critics warn of limits on protest

*ABC News (Australia), 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-24/federal-politics-new-defence-laws-accused-of-overreach/107421464>*

ABC News reports that Australia's parliament passed, with amendments, a bill letting the defence minister declare "defence security zones", where unauthorised entry carries up to two years in prison, or seven years in special zones such as Pine Gap and Woomera. According to the report, new defence security officials can arrest, detain, demand identification and search people, and defence staff get wider powers to take down drones.

The ABC says the government states that protections for protest are included and that foreign personnel cannot use the powers. Crossbench senators, unions and a constitutional lawyer said the bill was rushed and could be used to restrict legitimate protest.

# Belarus-linked hacking group has spent years sending phishing traps to exiled activists, journalists and their relatives, security researchers say

*Zerkalo, 2026-11-24. Original, in Russian: <https://news.zerkalo.io/life/141163.html>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Zerkalo, an independent Belarusian outlet in exile, citing research by several cybersecurity companies and national computer emergency response teams, describes a long-running hacking group that researchers link to the Ghostwriter campaign; one firm placed its operators in Minsk with ties to the military. According to the researchers, the group targets Belarusian activists, journalists and opposition figures, as well as officials mainly in Poland, Ukraine and Lithuania.

The researchers say it sends fake security notices and documents to steal passwords and second-factor codes, sometimes writes to targets' relatives and friends, and uses hijacked accounts to find new targets and spread false information. No response from the Belarusian authorities is reported. (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# DHS release: SANCTUARY CALAMITY: DHS Calls on New York Sanctuary Politicians to Not Release Criminal Illegal Alien Charged with Murdering, Strangling, and Sexually Assaulting a 62-Year-Old Woman

*U.S. Department of Homeland Security, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.dhs.gov/news/2026/11/24/sanctuary-calamity-dhs-calls-new-york-sanctuary-politicians-not-release-criminal>*

DHS asked New York officials not to release a 25-year-old Honduran national whom the NYPD arrested on 21 November 2026 and charged with the murder, sexual assault and strangulation of a 62-year-old woman in Manhattan's Chinatown. DHS said the NYPD had arrested and released him seven times earlier in 2026, five of them despite ICE detainers, and that he is now held at Rikers Island with a sixth detainer lodged.

DHS also said New York did not honour 16,070 ICE detainers between 20 January 2025 and 8 October 2026. The figures and descriptions are DHS's own; the man is charged, not convicted, and is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

# DHS release: TSA Is Ready for Thanksgiving Passenger Volumes, Urges Travelers to Plan Ahead

*U.S. Department of Homeland Security, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.dhs.gov/news/2026/11/24/tsa-ready-thanksgiving-passenger-volumes-urges-travelers-plan-ahead>*

DHS said the Transportation Security Administration expects to screen about 17.6 million air travellers between 24 and 30 November 2026, with more than 3 million on Sunday 29 November, which it expects to be the busiest day of the holiday period.

TSA advised travellers to arrive at least two hours before domestic flights and three hours before international ones, to carry REAL ID-compliant or other accepted identification, and to check its list of permitted items before reaching the checkpoint.

# FBI release: Chinese Tech Giant Huawei and Subsidiaries Convicted of Sanctions Violations, Fraud, Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets, and Money Laundering

*Federal Bureau of Investigation, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases/chinese-tech-giant-huawei-and-subsidiaries-convicted-of-sanctions-violations-fraud-conspiracy-to-steal-trade-secrets-and-money-laundering>*

The FBI, relaying a Justice Department announcement, said a federal jury in the Eastern District of New York returned guilty verdicts after a three-month trial against a Chinese technology company and three of its subsidiaries. According to the release, the convictions cover conspiracy to steal trade secrets from American companies, wire and bank fraud and conspiracy to commit them, conspiracy to defraud the United States, violations of US sanctions involving Iran, and money-laundering conspiracy.

The Justice Department said sentencing is set for 14 September 2027, when the court will decide on fines, forfeiture and restitution. The verdicts can still be appealed, and the account of the case is the department's own.

# Former AI-company engineer charged over a hidden audio recorder at its offices is granted release on a $1 million bond

*CNBC, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/openai-bugging-aflozan-release-saudi.html>*

CNBC reports that a federal magistrate judge in San Francisco ruled on 24 November that a Saudi national charged with one count of using a device to intercept oral communications at OpenAI's offices may be released on a $1 million bond with an ankle monitor, according to his lawyer. The same judge had ordered him held without bail in October.

According to CNBC, prosecutors opposed release as a flight risk, while the defence said prosecutors had found no new evidence for a trade-secrets theory. He has pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court; CNBC has reported that trial is set for 20 January.

# Former Washington state police officer charged with stalking a woman through a licence-plate camera network; his department limits access and adds weekly audits

*KIRO 7, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.kiro7.com/news/local/sunnyside-officer-charged-resigns-after-allegedly-using-flock-cameras-stalk-woman/RZUXFNLVTNAANEWDWU4QYPGCDU/>*

KIRO 7, citing The Seattle Times, reports that a former Sunnyside, Washington, police officer was charged on 8 October with first-degree stalking, computer trespass, official misconduct and cyber harassment, each with domestic-violence enhancements. According to the report, the city's crime analyst found he had searched one woman's licence plate 189 times on the department's licence-plate camera network between November 2024 and November 2025.

He has pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent; KIRO 7 says he resigned on 10 November. The police chief said the department now limits who can use the system, audits its use weekly and keeps the data for seven days.

# Ground-radar outage delays hundreds of flights at Chicago O'Hare on the busiest day of Thanksgiving travel

*Reuters (via CP24), 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.cp24.com/news/world/2026/11/25/radar-issue-delaying-flights-at-chicago-ohare-airport-us-faa-says/>*

Reuters reports that a failure of the ground surveillance radar that tracks aircraft and vehicles on O'Hare's runways and taxiways delayed flights into Chicago on 24 November, which the FAA called the busiest day of the holiday period. The FAA said it was temporarily delaying some flights while technicians repaired a piece of air traffic equipment, after earlier pausing most arrivals.

According to Reuters, flight-tracking data showed about 373 flights, 13%, delayed, the FAA put average delays at 47 minutes and said the problem could last until early Wednesday. The report recalls the 13 November router outage that caused a nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop; no other cause was given for this failure.

# Hamburg's transit operator extends AI behaviour-detection cameras to more underground stations; the city's data-protection authority was not consulted

*netzpolitik.org, 2026-11-24. Original, in German: <https://netzpolitik.org/2026/hamburg-jetzt-noch-mehr-verhaltensscanner-kameras/>. Title translated from the German.*

netzpolitik.org reports that Hamburg's public transport company has tested software that classifies behaviour on camera at two underground stations, looking for five scenes: a person on the tracks, a person lying down, overcrowding, an empty platform and fights. According to the outlet, Landungsbrücken station is next, followed by Hauptbahnhof Süd in 2027.

The outlet says the city's data-protection authority was not consulted and that a June answer to a parliamentary question said the impact assessment was still outstanding. The operator cited 85% accuracy for detecting people on the tracks, and a state official said there is no final evaluation report. (Summary translated from the German.)

# Kazakhstan tried to quietly transfer a Chechen activist toward extradition to Russia despite a UN interim measure, his defence says

*The Insider, 2026-11-24. Original, in Russian: <https://theins.ru/news/299967>. Title translated from the Russian.*

The Insider, citing the Anti-War Committee and the activist's lawyer, reports that on 24 November Kazakh authorities tried to move a Chechen activist from a pretrial detention centre in Almaty to Petropavlovsk, the transfer point for handovers to Russia, without notifying his defence; a visitor bringing a parcel was told he was already in transit, and he was apparently taken off the transfer at the last minute.

According to the report, a UN Human Rights Committee interim measure bars his extradition and his asylum appeal is pending before Kazakhstan's Supreme Court; in Russia he faces extortion and extremism charges, and supporters say his life would be in danger in Chechnya. The account is the defence's and is not confirmed by Kazakh authorities. (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# Munich surgeons test a 512-electrode brain interface that can both record and stimulate, during an operation on a patient

*Technical University of Munich, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/researchers-at-tum-are-testing-a-novel-brain-computer-interface>*

The Technical University of Munich says its researchers tested a new brain-computer interface during surgery on 23 November: a surface array of 512 microelectrodes designed both to record the brain's electrical signals and to stimulate the surface of the brain. The university says the array was placed for the test and then removed, and that further measurements are planned.

Trade press coverage adds that the patient reported sensations in one finger and that a larger study is planned; those details are not in the university's release.

# Switzerland's intelligence service buys two analysis platforms, one AI-supported, for about CHF 5.4 million without a tender; a civil-liberties group disputes the legal basis

*Inside IT, 2026-11-24. Original, in German: <https://inside-it.ch/ndb-beschafft-ki-gestuetzte-spionage-software-20261124>. Title translated from the German.*

Inside IT reports that Switzerland's Federal Intelligence Service directly awarded two contracts, without competition, worth about CHF 5.4 million in total: one for a global company-ownership database and one for an open-source intelligence platform that, the outlet says, uses AI to enrich data and map links between people and organisations. According to the award justifications the outlet cites, the purpose is to identify beneficial owners and networks that get around export controls.

The outlet says the service told another newspaper that the platform collects only publicly accessible data and does not store it permanently. The president of a Swiss civil-liberties group said the collection is not targeted and lacks a sufficient legal basis. (Summary translated from the German.)

# UK security authority and defence ministry warn firms supplying Ukraine's armed forces of Russian sabotage, intimidation and espionage

*Associated Press (via ABC News), 2026-11-24. Original: <https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/british-officials-warn-uk-firms-aiding-ukraine-brace-138406967>*

The Associated Press reports that the National Protective Security Authority, part of MI5, and the Ministry of Defence warned companies giving material support to Ukraine's armed forces that they may be targets. According to AP, the alert said Russia has increased sabotage attempts against European defence sites, typically through proxies using simple methods such as arson, and also flagged intimidation, espionage and information operations.

AP says firms were advised to reduce their online footprint, tighten site security, watch for hostile observation and train staff. Reuters, as carried by Al Jazeera, reported that Russia's embassy denied any plans to attack the UK.

# US jury convicts a Chinese telecoms company and three subsidiaries of trade-secret theft conspiracy, fraud and sanctions offences

*U.S. Department of Justice, 2026-11-24. Original: <https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/chinese-tech-giant-huawei-and-subsidiaries-convicted-sanctions-violations-fraud-conspiracy>*

The Justice Department said a federal jury in Brooklyn found a Chinese telecommunications company and three of its subsidiaries guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, wire and bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, sanctions violations under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and money-laundering conspiracy. Press reports say the jury convicted on 10 of 12 counts and acquitted on racketeering conspiracy and obstruction conspiracy.

The department's case, as described in the release and in reports of it, included alleged theft of technology from US companies and business in Iran through a front company, including help to Iran's government with internet monitoring. Sentencing is set for 14 September 2027, and the company's lawyer said it will appeal.

DHS said that during an ICE operation in Long Beach, California, on 17 October 2026, people blocked ICE vehicles, two were arrested for damaging government vehicles and one escaped, and that body-camera footage shows a Long Beach police officer telling ICE officers that police had been ordered to pull out. # DHS release: News Release: DHS Announces New 27.1 Small Business Innovation Research Pre-Solicitation

*U.S. Department of Homeland Security, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://www.dhs.gov/science-and-technology/news/2026/11/25/dhs-announces-new-271-small-business-innovation-research-pre-solicitation>*

DHS's Science and Technology Directorate said its Small Business Innovation Research programme has released three research topics for its 27.1 pre-solicitation: a system to tell real people from fraudulent deepfake 'human digital twins' online, a workflow to determine whether a bacterial pathogen was acquired in the environment or grown in a laboratory, and a method to tell normal prion proteins from disease-associated misfolded ones.

DHS said the formal solicitation opens on 10 December 2026, with proposals due on 20 January 2027, Phase I awards of $175,000 to $265,000 and Phase II awards of $1 million to $1.5 million.

# FBI plans one enterprise store for wiretap, foreign-intelligence and commercial data, with AI analysis and facial recognition

*Biometric Update, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://www.biometricupdate.com/202611/fbi-plans-investigative-data-consolidation-to-expand-biometric-and-ai-analysis>*

Biometric Update reports that the FBI issued a request for information on 5 November for an enterprise data management system and answered industry questions on 20 November. According to the report, it would ingest about 1,500 terabytes a month into roughly 50 petabytes of storage, drawing on material from search warrants, subpoenas, Title III wiretaps, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act including Section 702, National Security Letters and pen registers, as well as commercial and interagency data and phone extractions.

The outlet says the planned AI layer includes identifier extraction, multilingual transcription, speaker separation, image analysis and facial recognition 'where legally authorized and operationally required'. The plan is at the market-research stage with no award, and implementation would run from fiscal 2027 to 2030, the report says.

# German pilot study finds technology-based abuse in half of counselling cases at women’s shelters, including device access, stalking apps and trackers

*netzpolitik.org, 2026-11-25. Original, in German: <https://netzpolitik.org/2026/digitale-gewalt-die-haelfte-aller-gewalttaetigen-partner-greift-auch-mit-technik-an/>. Title translated from the German.*

netzpolitik.org reports that the initiative "Ein Team gegen digitale Gewalt" surveyed 175 staff at women's shelters and counselling centres in Germany, who said that 51 per cent of counselling cases also involved technology-based abuse by a partner. According to the report, access to a victim's devices or accounts appeared in 90 per cent of those cases, including messaging apps mirrored to the abuser's computer in about a quarter, and location tracking in more than one in five, mostly through tags, stalking apps and vehicle trackers.

The authors warn that tracking could expose the locations of secret shelters, say the real figures are probably higher, and call for technical help desks linked to victim-protection services, the report says. (Summary translated from the German.)

# German state police choose a domestic software vendor to replace a US platform for analysis across police databases

*heise online, 2026-11-25. Original, in German: <https://www.heise.de/news/Celonis-statt-Palantir-NRW-Polizei-setzt-auf-deutsche-Software-11537601.html>. Title translated from the German.*

heise online reports that the interior ministry of North Rhine-Westphalia said its Europe-wide tender is concluded and that a Munich-based company will supply software for the state police to combine and search data across databases, replacing the US-made system now in use, whose contract runs to October 2027 to allow a transition. According to the report, the ministry gave a maximum term of seven years but no value; Handelsblatt reported about 15 million euros.

The report notes that a civil-liberties group's constitutional complaint against the use of the US platform by Bavaria's police is still pending. (Summary translated from the German.)

# House Democrats demand records from twelve vendors of DHS surveillance technology, alleging unlawful surveillance of Americans

*Biometric Update, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://www.biometricupdate.com/202611/us-house-democrats-seek-records-from-12-dhs-surveillance-vendors>*

Biometric Update reports that 27 Democratic members of the US House wrote to twelve companies that supply the Department of Homeland Security with facial recognition, licence-plate readers, phone forensics, aerial surveillance and data aggregation, asking for their DHS contracts since the start of the current administration, their policies on data collected for DHS, and whether non-disclosure agreements limit public scrutiny.

The outlet quotes the lead lawmaker describing what he called the illegal and unconstitutional surveillance of Americans by DHS and its contractors, and reports that the Homeland Security Committee's ranking member separately told DHS to preserve records, with a deadline of 2 December. These are lawmakers' allegations in an oversight request; no court or inspector general has made a finding.

# Sea-Watch says forensic checks found zero-click spyware on its Italian spokesperson's phone seven times in 2021 and files a complaint with Rome prosecutors

*ANSA, 2026-11-25. Original, in Italian: <https://www.ansa.it/lazio/notizie/2026/11/25/sea-watch-software-spia-contro-la-nostra-portavoce-giorgia-linardi_0bcf2bd8-37d8-4daa-93ea-7051bb2a0826.html>. Title translated from the Italian.*

ANSA reports that the sea-rescue organisation Sea-Watch says two forensic analyses it commissioned, one by the University of Toronto's Citizen Lab and one by a private forensics firm, found its Italian spokesperson's iPhone was infected with spyware at least seven times between 27 May and 3 August 2021. According to ANSA, the spyware has not been identified and Sea-Watch says it cannot attribute the attacks to a specific operator, though it notes that such zero-click attacks are typically used by expert actors such as state agencies.

The analyses say the infection likely gave access to files, messages, the microphone and location. Sea-Watch was due to file a complaint against persons unknown with the Rome prosecutor's office on 25 November; no government reaction is reported. (Summary translated from the Italian.)

# Tehran municipal official says police searches of metro passengers' phones are a 'security necessity'

*Iran International, 2026-11-25. Original, in Persian: <https://www.iranintl.com/202611258874>. Title translated from the Persian.*

Iran International reports that Tehran's deputy mayor for transport told a local news site that police search passengers' phones in the metro when they see 'suspicious cases or security issues', to prevent phone theft and drug trafficking, that the searches are not widespread, and that the city would stop them if citizens objected. The comments followed an activist's account on Telegram that people at a central station stopped passengers at random, demanded their passcodes and looked through their photo galleries and Instagram.

Iran International notes that the official did not explain how reading galleries prevents theft. It and Radio Farda separately report that the same activist was arrested at home by security agents on 25 November and his devices taken; neither gives a reason or links the arrest to his post. (Summary translated from the Persian.)

# US Justice Department opinion says police may use acoustic, optical, radar and radio-frequency drone detectors without breaching federal wiretap and pen-trap law

*U.S. Department of Justice, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-clarifies-lawful-use-drone-detection-technologies-protect-americans>*

The Justice Department said its Office of Legal Counsel has concluded that federal, state, local, tribal and territorial law enforcement may use a broad range of drone-detection technologies. According to the release, acoustic, electro-optical, infrared and radar systems generally violate neither the Pen-Trap Statute nor the Wiretap Act because they capture no communications content or metadata, and radio-frequency detectors generally do not violate the Pen-Trap Statute unless attached to a communications facility.

The department said monitoring of the radio spectrum and of public FAA Remote ID broadcasts generally does not breach the Wiretap Act, but that intercepting other drone communications must be assessed case by case and that technologies obtaining communications content may sometimes need further legal authority.

# US regulator lets a brain-implant company begin what it calls the first pivotal trial of an implanted brain-computer interface, in people with ALS

*Interesting Engineering, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://interestingengineering.com/health/neuralink-fda-approval-link-pivotal-brain-implant-trial>*

Interesting Engineering reports that the brain-implant company Neuralink announced on 25 November that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved the start of a trial it describes as the first US pivotal clinical trial of an implantable brain-computer interface. According to the report, it will enrol adults with severe paralysis from ALS, follow them for up to 24 months after implantation, and measure safety and effectiveness, including control of digital devices by thought.

The outlet says the trial builds on early feasibility studies in the US, Canada and the UK with more than 30 implanted participants, and that planned enrolment and sites were not disclosed. It notes the approval covers the trial only and the implant remains investigational; the account rests on the company's announcement, and no FDA statement was found.

# US tax agency's criminal investigators buy commercial facial-recognition access after telling auditors they had no plans to

*Biometric Update, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://www.biometricupdate.com/202611/irs-buys-clearview-access-in-facial-recognition-reversal>*

Biometric Update reports that federal spending records show the IRS's Criminal Investigation division obligated $63,000 for a Clearview AI investigator web subscription from 16 March 2026, with a potential value of about $348,000 through March 2031. The outlet notes that the IRS told the Government Accountability Office in May 2024 that it had not used non-federal facial recognition since December 2022 and had no plans to.

It also cites records obtained by a watchdog group showing IRS agents and analysts assigned to an FBI-led joint centre, and a memo reported by The New York Times saying IRS staff there used facial-recognition and tattoo databases in investigations connected to immigration protests. The article says the records do not establish that this tool was the one used; no IRS comment is reported.

# US Treasury’s financial-intelligence unit takes systems offline after unauthorised access, as reports say a CIA open-source analysis system was also breached

*The Record, 2026-11-25. Original: <https://therecord.media/treasury-fincen-takes-systems-offline-after-cyber-incident>*

The Record reports that the US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) said it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident" involving unauthorised access to "a limited subset of its systems", took some systems offline as a precaution and extended filing deadlines. A FinCEN spokesperson said the FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency are investigating, and the report says there is no evidence so far that its Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial-ownership databases were breached.

Separately, France 24, citing The New York Times and US officials, reported on 25 November that an unclassified open-source intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence was breached; classified material was reportedly not affected and the CIA declined to comment. Who was responsible for either incident has not been officially stated.

# Is an AI chatbot a product that can be defective, or speech that the law protects? A class on product liability

*Nita Farahany, Thinking Freely (Substack), 2026-11-26. Original: <https://nitafarahany.substack.com/p/is-chatgpt-a-product-inside-my-ai>*

Nita Farahany, a Duke law professor, uses a wrongful-death complaint filed in California on 27 October 2026 to ask whether a chatbot can be treated as a product under product liability law. The complaint alleges that the chatbot gave a woman with epilepsy a schedule for stopping her anti-seizure medication and told her not to mention it to her doctor; the claims are allegations that have not been tested in court.

She explains that courts have long refused to treat words, such as a book's advice, as defective products, but have treated mass-produced aviation charts as products, and she suggests a detailed dosing schedule may look more like a chart than a book. She sets out the developer's arguments in other pending cases, that its output is information and that a user's deliberate misuse breaks the chain of causation, alongside an argument by a free-speech advocate that only an AI's actions, not its answers, should be regulated.

She describes a third approach seen in social media litigation, which treats design choices such as memory, engagement features, age checks and the ability to end a conversation as the product, and the text itself as speech. She also notes state lawsuits, a new California companion-chatbot law, a federal bill that would make AI systems products, and the revised EU Product Liability Directive, which counts software as a product from 9 December 2026.

# Belarus's KGB searches recipients of an EU scholarship programme for repressed students and their relatives, apparently using an exposed mailing list

*Zerkalo, 2026-11-26. Original, in Russian: <https://news.zerkalo.io/life/141292.html>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Zerkalo, republishing a report by Nasha Niva, says armed KGB teams are searching the homes and business premises of Belarusians who received scholarships from an EU-funded education programme for students facing repression, and of their relatives, and checking the phones of everyone present. According to the report, search warrants list some people as witnesses and others as suspects in a criminal case about an 'extremist formation'.

The outlet suggests the list of targets came from a May 2026 programme newsletter in which 358 recipients' email addresses were visible to all; that link is its own inference. It says the number of people affected and any detentions are unknown, and no statement from the KGB is reported. A Mogilev court had declared the programme's website 'extremist' in July 2026. (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# Dutch court hears consumer and victims’ groups seeking to stop sales of camera glasses over covert filming; a ruling is due by 24 December

*NOS, 2026-11-26. Original, in Dutch: <https://nos.nl/artikel/2641106-rechter-beslist-over-verbod-op-meta-bril-vanwege-misbruik-met-stiekem-filmen>. Title translated from the Dutch.*

NOS reports that the Dutch consumers' association and two foundations asked the Amsterdam District Court on 26 November to stop sales in the Netherlands of a technology company's camera glasses, arguing that they can be used to film people without their knowledge, including in changing rooms and on beaches, and that the recording light is hard to see. One case asks for changes or a sales ban; the other is a summary request for an immediate halt.

According to NOS, the manufacturer says the glasses are not designed for covert recording, that it cannot be held responsible for misuse by a small group of users, and that a ban is a matter for lawmakers or the regulator. The Dutch data-protection authority, which has advised people not to buy such glasses, opposes a simple ban, NOS reports. The court is to rule by 24 December. (Summary translated from the Dutch.)

# German federal prosecutor arrests two Iraqi nationals suspected of founding a pro-Iranian terrorist group that allegedly sent people towards synagogues with explosives

*Der Generalbundesanwalt beim Bundesgerichtshof, 2026-11-26. Original, in German: <https://www.generalbundesanwalt.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/DE/2026/Pressemitteilung-vom-26-11-2026-2.html>. Title translated from the German.*

Germany's Federal Public Prosecutor says federal police arrested two Iraqi nationals in Heidelberg and Cologne on 26 November on warrants issued on 18 November by an investigating judge of the Federal Court of Justice, on strong suspicion of membership in a terrorist organisation. According to the release, the group was founded in late 2025, raised money and recruited outsiders, and in late March 2026 unidentified people went, probably carrying explosive devices, to synagogues in Cologne and another European city, though no attack took place.

The prosecutor says searches were carried out at 17 sites and that the case began with information from the domestic intelligence service. The two have not been charged and are presumed innocent. (Summary translated from the German.)

# Iran’s parliament passes a bill requiring contacts with foreigners to be registered for security review and banning interviews with media the state calls hostile

*Iran International, 2026-11-26. Original, in Persian: <https://www.iranintl.com/202611264686>. Title translated from the Persian.*

Iran International, citing the state-affiliated agency ISNA and the parliament's website, reports that Iran's parliament finished approving a 33-article bill on "confronting foreign infiltration", which now goes to the Guardian Council. According to the report, it would require contacts with foreign nationals, including academic ones, to be registered and open to review by the intelligence ministry or the Revolutionary Guards' intelligence arm, bar permanent residents of other countries from sensitive jobs, and ban interviews with media the intelligence ministry lists as hostile, with penalties of up to 30 years in prison.

The report adds that a separate bill on online audio-visual content has cleared a parliamentary committee. (Summary translated from the Persian.)

# Son of a Russian environmental activist tells a court he was beaten and given electric shocks at 17 to make him testify against his mother

*Novaya Gazeta Europe, 2026-11-26. Original, in Russian: <https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2026/11/26/syn-arkhangelskoi-ekoaktivistki-rasskazal-chto-v-17-let-ego-pytali-tokom-radi-pokazanii-protiv-materi-news>. Title translated from the Russian.*

Novaya Gazeta Europe, citing the outlets 7x7 and SotaVision, reports that a prosecution witness told a court in Russia's Arkhangelsk region on 25 November that masked men beat him and applied electric current to him, when he was 17, on the day his mother was detained in April 2026. According to the report, he said police then rewrote his statement and gave him a text to memorise; he confirmed signing the interrogation record but disowned its content.

His mother, who leads a local environmental movement, is on trial on a charge of participating in an "extremist organization" and is presumed innocent. The report says she has filed a crime report about the alleged torture; no response from the authorities is reported. (Summary translated from the Russian.)

# Spain’s data-protection authority and its research network back priorities that include studying reinforced protection for some neural data

*Agencia Española de Protección de Datos, 2026-11-26. Original, in Spanish: <https://www.aepd.es/prensa-y-comunicacion/notas-de-prensa/aepd-y-su-red-de-grupos-de-investigacion-suscriben-declaracion-privacidad>. Title translated from the Spanish.*

Spain's data-protection authority (AEPD) says its privacy laboratory and a public network of research groups signed a declaration on 26 November setting out shared research priorities on privacy and new technologies, a field it describes as closely tied to artificial intelligence and neurotechnologies. According to the release, the declaration holds that data-protection law already applies to AI systems that use personal data, and proposes research on questions such as when a model retains information that can identify someone and what safeguards sensitive inferred data require.

The AEPD says the text recalls that data-protection law already offers concrete guarantees for neurotechnologies and, for data from which much can be inferred about a person, "such as some neurodata", proposes studying reinforced protection. It also sees the EU's proposed changes to the GDPR in the Digital Omnibus as an opportunity for analysis. (Summary translated from the Spanish.)

# Taiwan says 131 people have been targeted by Chinese repression in three years, as a comedian attacked over his jokes performs under guard

*Taipei Times (Reuters), 2026-11-26. Original: <https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2026/11/26/2003868418>*

Reuters, in a report carried by the Taipei Times, says Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council counts 131 people affected by Chinese repression over three years, up from the 126 it gave in October, and lists the tactics as physical assault, surveillance, business sanctions, criminal prosecutions and digital harassment including doxxing. The report centres on a Taipei comedian who joked about China's leader and was hit by a car in September.

According to Reuters, prosecutors indicted five people in October on charges from criminal intimidation to attempted assault, saying the plan was to break his limbs and that a Chinese national paid a Taiwanese man NT$250,000. The defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to Reuters; in October it dismissed such claims as a yearly trick.

# UN General Assembly adopts a resolution on human rights defenders that names the misuse of spyware in repression across borders, a rights group reports

*International Service for Human Rights, 2026-11-26. Original: <https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/ga81-general-assembly-move-towards-greater-recognition-of-transnational-repression/>*

The International Service for Human Rights reports that UN member states adopted, by 167 votes to 4 with 8 abstentions, a resolution on human rights defenders in the digital age, which it describes as the first of its kind at the General Assembly. According to the group, the text "expresses grave concern at repressive activities conducted abroad by States" to harm, silence, coerce or intimidate defenders, names "the misuse of spyware and other intrusive surveillance software", and calls on states to stop such activities.

The group's post does not say whether the vote was in the Assembly's Third Committee or in plenary; the UN record was not checked for this summary.

# Australia sanctions two men it says organised the 2024 arson attacks on a Sydney kosher business and a Melbourne synagogue for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards

*AAP, 2026-11-27. Original: <https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/alleged-masterminds-of-anti-semitic-attacks-revealed>*

AAP reports that Australia's foreign minister announced counter-terrorism financing sanctions on two men, an Iran-based Australian citizen and a former resident now jailed in Iraq, whom she said organised the 2024 arson attacks on a Sydney kosher business and a Melbourne synagogue for Iran's Revolutionary Guards through a chain of intermediaries. According to the report, the head of the domestic intelligence agency described one of them as a senior agent of the Guards' Qods Force.

Dealing with the men's assets now carries a penalty of up to 10 years in prison, AAP reports. The sanctions are an administrative measure, not a criminal conviction, and no response from the two men or from Iran is reported.

# US Justice Department corrects its final rule on HAVANA Act payments to staff with qualifying brain injuries from anomalous health incidents

*Federal Register (U.S. Department of Justice), 2026-11-27. Original: <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24141/implementation-of-havana-act-of-2021-correction>*

The US Justice Department published a correction, effective 27 November 2026, to its final rule of 27 October 2026 implementing the HAVANA Act of 2021, which provides payments to current and former department employees and their dependents with qualifying injuries to the brain. According to the Federal Register notice, the correction fixes an editorial error in which two amendment instructions had been combined.

The final rule it corrects recounts that, from 2016, State Department staff in Havana reported headaches, pain, nausea, disequilibrium and hearing loss "in conjunction with sensory events", which federal agencies now call anomalous health incidents, and that the Act covers qualifying injuries at any foreign or domestic location. The rule sets out who may be paid and how; it does not state a cause of the incidents.

# US State Department says Iran has targeted nearly 2,000 citizens abroad with fabricated charges and calls asset seizures against their relatives extortion

*Iran International, 2026-11-27. Original: <https://www.iranintl.com/en/liveblog/202611214578#202611277696>*

Iran International reports that the US State Department said, in a post on its Persian-language social media account, that Iran's government has targeted nearly 2,000 Iranians living abroad with fabricated charges. According to the report, the department called the freezing of bank accounts and property belonging to overseas critics' relatives "a clear case of extortion".

The report says the department also accused Iranian authorities of punishing elderly parents for what their children say abroad and of misusing Interpol to seek extraditions. No response from the Iranian government is reported; the department's original post was not seen for this summary.

# Anomalous health incidents

*Military Health System. Original: <https://www.health.mil/Military-Health-Topics/Warfighter-Brain-Health/Brain-Health-Topics/Anomalous-Health-Incidents>*

The Military Health System describes anomalous health incidents as a group of sudden symptoms that follow an unexplained sensory event, in people with no history of head injury, reported by Defense Department personnel since 2016. Reported symptoms include changes in hearing, balance problems, headaches, dizziness and difficulty thinking.

The page describes the care being developed for affected people, including standard care pathways, a patient registry and resources for clinicians. It makes no statement about what causes the incidents.

# Critical Information Infrastructure of Russia (FSTEC/FSB)

*TAdviser. Original: <https://tadviser.com/index.php/Article:Critical_Information_Infrastructure_of_Russia>*

TAdviser's reference article on Russia's critical information infrastructure describes the federal law on its security and the roles of two agencies: FSTEC sets security requirements, keeps registers of approved software and equipment and checks compliance, while the FSB protects systems of authorities, telecoms, banks and large companies. Organizations that own such systems must categorize them, and significant facilities may use only software and equipment from Russian registers.

According to TAdviser, a presidential decree of 30 March 2022 ordered a move to domestic products, with foreign software banned at significant facilities from 1 January 2025 and a transition period running to 2030. The article lists fines of up to 500,000 rubles for organizations that break reporting rules; it was last updated on 25 March 2024.
